result.title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces
result.comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Code and data: https://github.com/hopit-ai/harness-mistakes-artifacts
result.summary: We evaluate whether an AI agent's harness, the notes around its model, can learn from the agent's failure traces beyond a matched search that never sees them. It can, but less than it looks. We tested an open 9-billion-parameter model with fixed weights; a larger teacher model wrote its notes. On generated customer-service decisions, where both note writers were told the target rules, notes based on the agent's mistakes improved accuracy by 4.0 percentage points over notes from the same process with the mistakes withheld. That process alone, trying and keeping better-scoring notes, reached about 60% of the total improvement. In full customer-service conversations the same notes showed no demonstrated improvement. Separately, a strict screen of single lessons admitted two customer-service lessons, still awaiting tests on new data, and one tool-use lesson, written without seeing the agent's mistakes, which showed no demonstrated gain on new tool-use tasks. A neutral note with no procedure scored higher than the learned lessons (exploratory). A blind audit judged 146 of 240 tool-use test items defective.

AI.brief_summary: 在权重固定的 9B 模型上，由更大教师模型依据智能体的失败轨迹撰写 harness 笔记，并与「看不到失败轨迹」的同等笔记搜索对比，检验失败轨迹的增量价值，另对单条教训做严格筛选与测试项盲审。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把增益归因于失败轨迹本身、并指出搜索基线已占约六成改进的对照思路，可能为 LVR 中轨迹监督的贡献分配与评测效度核查提供概念借鉴，但与视觉或多模态推理无直接联系。
